name: auth-header
description:
REGRESSION LOCK on the X-Auth-Token header. Carbon Black documents the header as <API Secret Key>/<API ID>, secret first, with the Org Key appearing only in the request path. This script built it as <api_key>/<organization_key> and CONFIG declared no API ID parameter at all, so the API ID was never sent and no request could authenticate against a real tenant.

Every route here matches on the correct header and anything else falls through to a 401, which is what a real tenant does -- so a wrong header produces zero assets rather than a passing run. The three values are deliberately distinct strings with no shared substring: the secret is 'fixture-api-key', the API ID 'SYNAPIID01', the Org Key 'SYNORG01'. requests_absent then pins the Org Key OUT of the header while requests_include pins it INTO the path, which is the actual distinction the defect got wrong.

Both header construction sites are covered: the device scroll and the per-device vulnerability search each carry it independently.

Ids are asserted in the scoped carbon-black:<org_key>:<device id> form, so the header fixture also proves the Org Key that scopes the id is the one from the path, and the namespaced_ids invariant enforces the scheme.

vuln_info.cve_description: Synthetic fixture description for a remote code execution issue in a logging library.
vuln_info.solution: Upgrade the affected package to a fixed release.
